phrasings.literal: List every item, of any kind, that the legacy TGA import path task #247 is directly blocked by.
phrasings.short: direct blockers of #247, any kind
phrasings.paraphrased: Something has to be settled before #247 can proceed; name each thing it directly waits on, whether it is a task or not.

gold_query: CALL blockers(#247) YIELD blocker RETURN blocker
notes: SD §6: BLOCKS #225->#247 is the only edge into #247, and #225 is a question (QU-tga, open, SD §5.2). SD §11.5: blockers(#247) = (#225, 1, -, direct, false, -). A pattern that restricts the blocker to (b:task) returns nothing.

phrasings.literal: Which tasks must be finished at least two steps before #280 can start, counting only chains of direct prerequisites?
phrasings.short: indirect prerequisites of #280
phrasings.paraphrased: Before snapshot interpolation (#280) can begin, which work sits two or more dependency links upstream of it?

gold_query: MATCH (x:task)-[:BLOCKS]->{2,}(#280) RETURN x
notes: SD §6: TC-1 -> TC-2 -> TC-7 is a walk of length 2; TC-1 also blocks TC-7 directly (the shortcut), which does not remove it (walk semantics, [50 §3.7] rule 2).

phrasings.literal: Which tasks are subtasks of subtasks of the asset pipeline campaign #240, that is, exactly two levels below it in the task tree?
phrasings.short: tasks exactly two levels below #240
phrasings.paraphrased: In the hierarchy of campaign #240, list the grandchildren: the tasks whose parent's parent is #240.

gold_query: MATCH (#240)-[:PARENT_OF]->{2}(t) RETURN t
notes: SD §5.3 and §6 CHILD_OF: of the 13 children of #240 on main only #248 has children (#249, #250). CHILD_OF is a forest, so a walk of exactly two links is depth 2.

phrasings.literal: Which sections of the asset pipeline plan depend on the Manifest format section #255 through a chain of three or more dependency links? Count a section even if a shorter chain also links it to #255.
phrasings.short: sections depending on #255 through three or more links
phrasings.paraphrased: Following section dependencies backwards from #255, which sections sit at the far end of some dependency chain at least three links long, whether or not a shorter route exists too?

gold_query: MATCH (s:doc)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->{3,}(#255) RETURN s
notes: SD §6 DEPENDS_ON: #256->#255, #257->#256, #258->#257, #259->#258 and the shortcut #259->#255. Walks into #255: length 3 from #258 (#258->#257->#256->#255), length 4 from #259; #259 also depends on #255 directly, which does not remove it (walk semantics, [50 §3.7] rule 2).

phrasings.literal: How many different tasks is the import validation task #248 blocked by through a chain of two or more direct prerequisite links? Count each task once, however many chains lead from it.
phrasings.short: number of distinct tasks two-plus prerequisite links upstream of #248
phrasings.paraphrased: Counting tasks rather than routes, how many pieces of work sit at least two dependency steps upstream of #248?

gold_query: MATCH (#248)-[:BLOCKED_BY]->{2,}(x) RETURN count(*) AS upstream
notes: SD §6: #245->#248; #243->#245, #241->#245 (shortcut), #241->#243. Walks of length >= 2 into #248: #243->#245->#248, #241->#245->#248, #241->#243->#245->#248, so the endpoints are #243 and #241: 2 (a path count would give 3). count(*) over a quantified part counts endpoint pairs (N08, [50 §3.4] item 4).

phrasings.literal: Starting from #243 and following 'must finish before' links forward, but only into tasks that are still unfinished, which tasks can be reached?
phrasings.short: tasks reachable forward from #243 through unfinished tasks only
phrasings.paraphrased: Walk downstream from #243 along direct prerequisite links without ever stepping onto finished work: which tasks can you get to?

gold_query: MATCH (#243)((a)-[:BLOCKS]->(b:task) WHERE b.unfinished)+(t) RETURN t
notes: SD §6: #243->#245, #243->#244; #245->#246, #245->#248; no further links. SD §5.3/§11.1: #244 is done, #245, #246 and #248 are open, so the walk stops at #244. Without the per-step filter the answer would add #244.

phrasings.literal: Starting from #241 and following direct 'must finish before' links forward, which tasks can be reached by a chain of at least two links in which every task after #241 has an estimate recorded?
phrasings.short: tasks 2+ links downstream of #241 via estimated tasks only
phrasings.paraphrased: Going downstream from the manifest schema task #241 by two or more prerequisite hops, and passing only through tasks that carry an estimate, which tasks do you reach?

gold_query: MATCH (#241)((a)-[:BLOCKS]->(b:task) WHERE b.estimate IS NOT NULL){2,}(t) RETURN t
notes: SD §5.3 estimates: #245 8, #246 5; #243, #244 and #248 have none. SD §6: #241->#243 (no estimate, stop), #241->#245 (ok), #245->#246 (ok), #245->#248 (no estimate). The only qualifying walk of length >= 2 is #241->#245->#246. Unfiltered, {2,} would give #244, #245, #246, #248.

phrasings.literal: On the net lane (lane/net), starting from #276 and following 'must finish before' links forward, which tasks can be reached if you only step onto tasks that carry no unresolved merge conflict on that lane?
phrasings.short: lane/net: forward from #276, skipping conflicted tasks
phrasings.paraphrased: In the net lane's view, trace the work downstream of #276 but never pass through a task whose data is in merge conflict there. What do you reach?

gold_query: USE lane/net MATCH (#276)((a)-[:BLOCKS]->(b:task) WHERE NOT b.conflicted)+(t) RETURN t
notes: SD §6: #276->#277 and #276->#280, neither has onward BLOCKS links. SD §10 and §11.3: #277 is conflicted on lane/net (FieldEdit on its priority), #280 is not. On main, where nothing is conflicted, the answer would be #277 and #280.

phrasings.literal: How many different tasks can reach #280 through a chain of direct prerequisite links in which no task along the chain is currently claimed under a live lease? Count each task once.
phrasings.short: count distinct tasks upstream of #280 via unclaimed chains
phrasings.paraphrased: Skipping any prerequisite someone holds a live lease on, and not passing through it, how many distinct tasks lie upstream of #280 along prerequisite chains?

gold_query: MATCH (x:task)((a:task)-[:BLOCKS]->(b) WHERE NOT a.claimed)+(#280) RETURN count(*) AS upstream
notes: SD §8.1 and §11.1: claimed at NOW = #242, #264, #276 (live leases). SD §6 into #280: #274, #275, #276 (claimed, cut); into #275: #274. Endpoints #274 and #275: 2, although three walks qualify (#274->#280, #275->#280, #274->#275->#280). N08.

phrasings.literal: For each task anywhere in the asset pipeline campaign #240 that other tasks depend on, how many different tasks does it hold up, directly or through chains of direct prerequisite links?
phrasings.short: per #240 task: distinct tasks it holds up transitively
phrasings.paraphrased: Across campaign #240 at any depth, take every task that something waits on and count the distinct tasks downstream of it, at any distance.

gold_query: MATCH (b:task)-[:BLOCKS]->+(t) WHERE b IN subtree(#240) RETURN b, count(*) AS downstream

phrasings.literal: For each section of the asset pipeline plan #254, how many direct dependency links go out from it to other sections? Leave out sections that have none.
phrasings.short: outgoing direct dependency links per section of #254
phrasings.paraphrased: Section by section in plan #254, count the direct dependencies each section declares on other sections, skipping sections that declare none.

gold_query: MATCH (s:doc)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->() WHERE s IN children(#254) RETURN s, count(*) AS links
notes: SD §5.3 (sections #255-#259 under #254) and §6 DEPENDS_ON: #256->#255, #257->#256, #258->#257, #259->#258, #259->#255; #255 depends on nothing. One binding per matched edge, anonymous target included ([50 §3.4] rule 1), so #259 counts 2.

phrasings.literal: How many different direct subtasks of the asset pipeline campaign #240 are themselves a direct prerequisite of at least one other task?
phrasings.short: count #240's direct subtasks that directly block something
phrasings.paraphrased: Among the immediate subtasks of #240, on how many does at least one other task wait directly? Count tasks, not links.

gold_query: MATCH (t:task)-[:CHILD_OF]->(#240) WHERE EXISTS { (t)-[:BLOCKS]->() } RETURN count(*) AS tasks
notes: SD §5.3 and §6: children of #240 with a BLOCKS out-edge are #241 (2 links), #242 (1), #243 (2), #245 (2), #252 (1, c.gate-a7): 5 tasks, 8 links. The existence test makes the task the unit ([50 §2.9] Q6).

phrasings.literal: Show the whole task tree of the asset pipeline campaign #240, the campaign task itself included, with each task's depth below #240.
phrasings.short: task tree of #240 with depths
phrasings.paraphrased: Lay out campaign #240 as a hierarchy: every task in it, #240 itself at depth zero, and how deep each one sits.

gold_query: CALL subtree(#240, depth: 3)
notes: SD §5.3 and §6 CHILD_OF on main: 13 children of #240 (#241-#248, #251, #252, #253, #901, #902; cancelled ones included), and #249, #250 under #248: 16 rows with the root. #1400 exists only on lane/assets.

phrasings.literal: Какие задачи должны быть завершены, прежде чем можно будет взяться за задачу #251?
phrasings.short: что блокирует задачу #251
phrasings.paraphrased: Задача #251 пока не может стартовать. Какая работа должна закончиться раньше неё?

gold_query: CALL blockers(#251) YIELD blocker RETURN blocker
notes: SD §6: BLOCKS #252->#251 exists on main from c.gate-a7 (s93). SD §11.5: blockers(#251) = (#252, 1, -, direct, false, -).

phrasings.literal: Which tasks implement a decision that itself replaced an older decision?
phrasings.short: tasks implementing a decision that superseded another
phrasings.paraphrased: Which work items build on a decision that took over from an earlier decision?

gold_query: MATCH (t:task)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(d:decision)-[:SUPERSEDES]->(old:decision) RETURN t
notes: SD §6: IMPLEMENTS #245->#220, #261->#222, #275->#223; SUPERSEDES between decisions only #220->#221. #222 and #223 supersede nothing.

phrasings.literal: Какой заметкой была заменена заметка #236 — первый черновик именования шин микшера?
phrasings.short: чем заменена заметка #236
phrasings.paraphrased: Первый вариант заметки об именовании шин микшера (#236) устарел. Какая заметка пришла ему на смену?

gold_query: MATCH (#236)-[:SUPERSEDED_BY]->(n) RETURN n
notes: SD §5.2 (#236 superseded) and §6: SUPERSEDES #237->#236.

phrasings.literal: Among the rules that apply to the file src/audio/mixer.rs, which one replaced an older rule, and which rule did it replace?
phrasings.short: rules for src/audio/mixer.rs that replaced another rule, with the replaced one
phrasings.paraphrased: When editing src/audio/mixer.rs, which applicable rule is the newer version of an earlier rule, and what was that earlier rule?

gold_query: MATCH (r:rule)-[:SUPERSEDES]->(old) WHERE applies(r, 'src/audio/mixer.rs') RETURN r, old
notes: SD §5.2: #213 applies to src/** and so to src/audio/mixer.rs; SD §6: SUPERSEDES #213->#212 is the only SUPERSEDES edge leaving a rule.

phrasings.literal: Bench run #1701 ran in one of the lanes. After which lane is that lane scheduled to merge?
phrasings.short: lane that #1701's lane must merge after
phrasings.paraphrased: Take the lane where run #1701 executed: which other lane has to be merged before it?

gold_query: MATCH (#1701)-[:RUNS_IN]->(l:lane)-[:MERGE_AFTER]->(x:lane) RETURN x
notes: SD §6: RUNS_IN #1701->#700; MERGE_AFTER #700->#800 (lane a merges after lane b, [50 §2.5]).

phrasings.literal: Which rules are in contradiction with a rule that has been confirmed by a measurement?
phrasings.short: rules contradicting a measurement-confirmed rule
phrasings.paraphrased: A measurement backed up one of the rules; which rules clash with the rule it backed up?

gold_query: MATCH (r:rule)-[:CONFIRMED_BY]->(m:measurement), (r)-[:CONTRADICTS]-(o:rule) RETURN o
notes: SD §6: CONFIRMS #601->#215 is the only measurement confirming a rule; CONTRADICTS #215->#214 is symmetric ([50 §2.5]), so #214 matches whichever way the arrow is written.

phrasings.literal: Which notes mention, in their text, a node that has since been deleted?
phrasings.short: notes whose text mentions a deleted node
phrasings.paraphrased: Some notes name, by number in their body, something that no longer exists. Which notes are they?

gold_query: MATCH (n:note) WHERE EXISTS { (n)-[:MENTIONS]->(:DELETED) } RETURN n
notes: SD §5 bodies: only #238 (mentions #239, live) and #298 (mentions #293) contain '#'; SD §6 MENTIONS #298->#293 is kept into the tombstone after c.x1-delete. Historical edges into deleted nodes are traversable only into a :DELETED pattern ([50 §3.6]).

phrasings.literal: On the net lane (lane/net), which unresolved merge conflicts are there? For each, give its key, the node it is on and its conflict class.
phrasings.short: unresolved conflicts on lane/net: key, node, class
phrasings.paraphrased: After main was last synced into the net lane, which conflicts were left open there, on which nodes, and of what kind?

gold_query: USE lane/net CALL conflicts() YIELD key, node, class
notes: SD §10: c.sync-net left FieldEdit #277.priority and StatusFork #603.status on lane/net. No named entry: the named query conflicts runs on main (README §8), which has no conflict values.

phrasings.literal: On the audio lane (lane/audio), one plan section has an unresolved text conflict. Give the section and the three competing texts: the common base, the audio lane's version and main's version.
phrasings.short: lane/audio text conflict: node, base, lane and main texts
phrasings.paraphrased: The last sync of main into the audio lane left a clash in a section's wording. Which section is it, and what do the base, lane and main versions say?

gold_query: USE lane/audio CALL conflicts() YIELD node, base, ours, theirs

rows: Voices come from a fixed pool of 64.
Voices come from a fixed pool of 128.
Voices come from a growable pool that starts at 64.

notes: SD §10: TextHunk on #270.body from c.sync-audio; ours is the lane (c.audio-s2-edit, s61), theirs is main (c.main-s2-edit, s67).

phrasings.literal: На ветке lane/net приоритет задачи #277 остался в неразрешённом конфликте слияния. Каким он был в общей базе, какой он на самой ветке и какой на main?
phrasings.short: lane/net: конфликт приоритета #277 — база, ветка, main
phrasings.paraphrased: После синхронизации main в ветку lane/net приоритет #277 так и не согласован. Назови три значения: исходное, на ветке и на main.

gold_query: USE lane/net CALL conflicts() YIELD node, base, ours, theirs WHERE node = #277 RETURN base, ours, theirs
notes: SD §10: FieldEdit #277.priority, base 2, ours 3 (lane/net, c.net-c4-prio), theirs 0 (main, c.main-c4-prio).

phrasings.literal: What is stopping the staged merge of the assets lane into main from finishing? List each violation on its staging ref merge/lane/assets/from/main with its key and class.
phrasings.short: violations on staging ref merge/lane/assets/from/main
phrasings.paraphrased: The merge of lane/assets into main is staged on merge/lane/assets/from/main but stuck. Which violations does that staged sync report?

gold_query: USE merge/lane/assets/from/main CALL violations()
notes: SD §3.1 and §10: one DanglingEdge on the staging ref: main added #252 BLOCKS #251 (c.gate-a7) while lane/assets deleted #251 (replaced_by #1400).

phrasings.literal: On the net lane (lane/net), a finding carries an unresolved merge conflict. Which plan document does that finding concern, through the plan section it is about?
phrasings.short: lane/net: plan concerned by the conflicted finding
phrasings.paraphrased: One review finding on the net lane is stuck in a merge conflict; follow it to the section it discusses and name the plan that section belongs to.

gold_query: USE lane/net MATCH (f:finding)-[:ABOUT]->(s:doc)-[:CHILD_OF]->(p:doc) WHERE f.conflicted RETURN DISTINCT p
notes: SD §10 and §11.3: #603 is conflicted on lane/net (StatusFork); SD §6: ABOUT #603->#283, CHILD_OF #283->#282. The lane-only findings #1301-#1304 are not conflicted.

phrasings.literal: Which commits on the staging ref merge/lane/assets/from/main, which holds the staged merge of the assets lane into main, are not yet on main?
phrasings.short: commits on merge/lane/assets/from/main not yet on main
phrasings.paraphrased: The staged merge of lane/assets sits on merge/lane/assets/from/main. List the commits reachable from that ref but not from main.

gold_query: CALL log(main..merge/lane/assets/from/main)
notes: SD §3.1 and §7: c.staged-assets has parents c.assets-a7-replace (lane/assets tip) and c.filler-d11 (main~4, reachable from main); lane/assets forked after c.lane-assets-open with 3 own commits. No filler commit in the range (SD §16 item 13).

phrasings.literal: Preview a merge between main and the net lane (lane/net), restricted to the netcode snapshots campaign #273: which tasks show a status change on either side since the two branches' last common base, and what is the status before and after?
phrasings.short: merge preview main and lane/net, #273: status changes
phrasings.paraphrased: Before merging lane/net and main, check campaign #273: whose status differs from the last common base on either branch, and how?

gold_query: CALL diff(main...lane/net, scope: #273) YIELD node, aspect, before, after WHERE aspect = 'status'
notes: SD §3.1 and §11.6: lane/net absorbed main up to c.filler-d10, the common base. Lane side: #274 done (c.net-c1-done), #275 done (c.net-c2-done), #276 in_progress (c.net-c3-claim); #277's priority is a conflict value (field aspect). Main touched nothing under #273 after c.filler-d10 (SD §7 s93-s103).

phrasings.literal: Which commits would a merge of the shaders lane (lane/shaders) into main bring over, and when was each one made?
phrasings.short: commits lane/shaders would bring into main, with times
phrasings.paraphrased: Before lane/shaders is merged, list the commits it has that main lacks, with the time of each.

gold_query: CALL log(main..lane/shaders) YIELD commit, at
notes: SD §3.1 and §7: lane/shaders forked after c.lane-shaders-open and was never synced; its own commits are s73 c.shaders-x7-delete (D9 10:00) and s74 c.shaders-s1 (D9 10:30), D9 = 2026-06-10 (SD §2.1). No filler commit in the range.

phrasings.literal: If the q3 plan branch (plan/q3) were merged into main, which stored field values of tasks in the asset pipeline campaign #240 would it change, and from what to what?
phrasings.short: merge preview main and plan/q3, #240: field changes
phrasings.paraphrased: Previewing plan/q3 against main for campaign #240, which task fields differ from their last common base, with the old and new value?

gold_query: CALL diff(main...plan/q3, scope: #240) YIELD node, aspect, name, before, after WHERE aspect = 'field'
notes: SD §3.1: plan/q3 forked after c.hdoc-edit2 and its only commit c.plan-reprio (SD §7 s88) moves #278 under #285, adds BLOCKS #279->#278 and sets #246's priority 2->1; only the last is a field change under #240. Main's only change under #240 since c.hdoc-edit2 is the edge #252->#251 (c.gate-a7), an edge row.

phrasings.literal: On the net lane (lane/net), finding #1304 refutes another finding whose status is in an unresolved merge conflict there. What are that conflict's value at the common base, the net lane's value and main's value?
phrasings.short: lane/net: conflict values of the finding #1304 refutes
phrasings.paraphrased: Finding #1304 on the net lane argues against another finding, and that finding's status is stuck in a merge conflict. Give its base, lane and main values.

gold_query: USE lane/net MATCH (#1304)-[:REFUTES]->(f) CALL conflicts() YIELD node, base, ours, theirs WHERE node = f RETURN base, ours, theirs
notes: SD §4: #1304 exists only on lane/net (on main it yields N06). SD §6: REFUTES #1304->#603 (lane/net only). SD §10: StatusFork #603.status, base open, ours refuted (c.net-refute), theirs confirmed (c.main-fc1-confirm).
